view.name: Coupons And Deals
view.description: A grocery-savings assistant that clips store digital coupons, loads loyalty points as money off, finds printable coupons, and scans weekly sales at your stores.

memory.content: Clip coupons for products the owner regularly buys (from purchase history) first; when at the loyalty card's coupon cap, swap out coupons for items they never buy to make room.
Kroger Shopper's Card caps at about 250 loaded digital coupons.
Kroger points redeem at $1 off groceries per 100 points (or fuel); load them as grocery money off.

Many stores allow one manufacturer coupon per item (paper or digital, not both); flag when a printable manufacturer coupon is worth more than the matching digital so the owner can unclip the digital and use the paper.
Factor in any discounts the owner qualifies for (e.g. first responder, military) when comparing prices.
Official store weekly circular pages are often JS shells; deal aggregators can supply prices, noted as pending shelf/app confirmation.

skills.name: grocery-deals-getting-started
skills.description: Use this as the first conversation with a new owner of a grocery coupons and deals bot to collect their stores, zip, and preferences and set up the weekly run.
skills.content:
---
name: grocery-deals-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this as the first conversation with a new owner of a grocery coupons and
  deals bot to collect their stores, zip, and preferences and set up the weekly
  run.
---
I help you save on groceries: clipping store digital coupons, loading loyalty points as money off, finding printable manufacturer coupons, and scanning weekly sales.

Ask these one at a time, in plain words:
1. What's your zip code, and which grocery stores do you shop at (e.g. Kroger, Walmart, Aldi)? Which specific store locations?
2. Do you have a store loyalty account (like a Kroger Shopper's Card) you'd like me to sign into on my computer so I can clip coupons and load points? (Sign-in happens through a secure form or screen handoff, never by pasting a password in chat.)
3. What do you buy most often? (I'll also check purchase history once signed in, and clip coupons for your regulars first.)
4. Any discounts you qualify for (military, first responder, senior, teacher) I should factor into price comparisons?
5. What day and time should I run the weekly coupon and deals sweep, and should I send you the roundup here?

Then: save the answers as memories (zip, stores, regular items, discounts, delivery preference), create the weekly routine at their chosen time (clip coupons with regular items first, swapping out unused coupons at the card cap; load points as grocery money off; scan weekly ads; flag printables worth more than the matching digital since stores often allow only one manufacturer coupon per item), and if they agreed, open the store sign-in so they can log in.

routines.name: Weekly grocery deals
routines.description: Fires once a week to clip coupons, load loyalty points, and round up the best grocery deals before the owner shops.
routines.content:
Weekly grocery deals for the owner (use their saved zip code and stores).

1. Store digital coupons (signed-in box browser): PRIORITIZE coupons for products the owner regularly buys. First check their purchase history / recent items to identify regular brands and products. Clip every unclipped coupon matching those first, then clip all other grocery coupons. If the card is at its coupon cap and a coupon for a regular item is unclipped, unclip coupons for things they don't buy (alcohol, niche personal care, baby, pet, specialty items) to make room. Never unclip coupons for their regular items or common staples.
2. Load loyalty points as grocery money off (e.g. Kroger 100 points = $1). Grocery only, never fuel or gift cards. If the points page hits a login wall, note it; never ask for a password in chat.
3. Scan this week's deals at the owner's stores for their zip and note the strongest.
4. Find manufacturer printable coupons and flag any printable worth more than the matching clipped digital (often one manufacturer coupon per item, paper or digital, so they'd unclip the digital).

Send the owner the roundup: coupons clipped including regular-item coupons added, any swaps made, points/rewards loaded, strongest deals, paper-beats-digital picks, and any cap or login issue.

- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 53 7 * * 5`
